title: Restriction to embedded Boolean tapes
statement: Let $K,m$ be natural numbers, let $\Gamma,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $R$ be an $m$-work-tape Boolean Turing machine with states in $S$, let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding, and let $\iota:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$ be an embedding. For a Boolean input word $x$, consider a $K$-tape configuration $d$ over $\Gamma$ on the input obtained by applying $e$ to every bit of $x$. Assume every symbol stored anywhere on each tape indexed by $\iota$ lies in the image of $e$. Then $d$ is exactly the configuration formed by embedding the decoded Boolean configuration into the selected tapes via $\iota$, leaving all other tapes and head positions as in $d$, and prefixing the decoded configuration's output by $d$'s output.
